title: Tangled Tales - Gatekeeper Chronicles - Take a Look
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9cZh_IuGMyM

Daniel (@dungeondive) digs out an oddity: Tangled Tales: The Gatekeeper Chronicles, a Mattel choose-your-own-adventure played with a numbered deck of cards and an electronic reader. Each chapter comes with a chip card that slots into the machine. Instead of turning to a page, you press symbols (spider, potion, skull, book) and the reader announces which card comes next, accompanied by spooky sound effects. He moves his mic next to the machine so viewers can hear it.

He plays the opening of Nightmare Unleashed. Against your mother's wishes, your weird aunt has dragged you to her creepy library during a thunderstorm, and the lights go out. A flashlight from the lost-and-found, something slurping among the shelves, and a tentacled beast lead to a ring that tightens on your finger. In the basement he finds a mural of your family tree that starts with a wizard named Magnus and ends with you. A hidden crack needs the keys he didn't take.

He had assumed it was from the late 80s and is surprised to find it dates from 2005, shortly before smartphones arrived. He likes the little machine's storage slot for a travel deck, though admits a stack of real gamebooks would probably serve better. It sends him back to Lone Wolf, Fighting Fantasy and the woven-cover D&D gamebooks.

----

Tangled Tales wraps a gamebook in a 2005 electronic gadget. Do these hybrid gimmicks add anything for you, or is a plain book always better?
